How to read the map

Ability first. Grammar in service of real communication.

Each level is a destination. The “can do” panel describes useful evidence, not boxes to tick.

Grammar and vocabulary provide the tools. Published lessons open directly; the rest remain visible as the planned route.

Listening, reading, speaking, and writing stay connected. Progress means using language across skills.

A0Starter

Pre-A1 · Absolute Beginner

The very first contact with English. Learners build the alphabet, sounds, numbers and a handful of survival phrases — enough to say who they are and exchange a few words.

Guided study0–60 hrsGSE range10–21
After completing the level

A0 End-of-Level Diagnostic

Check the complete foundation and decide whether the learner is ready to begin A1.

Evidence of progress

The learner notices, chooses, builds, understands, and produces language across grammar, vocabulary, receptive skills, and real communication.

By the end of A0, a learner can…

  • Recognise and say the alphabet and numbers 0–100.
  • Give basic personal details: name, age, nationality.
  • Understand and use a small set of everyday greetings.
  • Fill in a simple form with name, address and date of birth.
Aa

Grammar

The verb to be (am / is / are)→Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)→Articles a / an→this / that / these / those→Regular plural nouns→Possessive adjectives (my, your, his…)→Question words: what, where, who, how→Cardinal numbers 0–100→
¶

Vocabulary & Topics

Greetings & introductions→The alphabet & spelling→Days, months, dates→Colours & basic adjectives→Family members→Classroom objects→Animals→Countries & nationalities→
01

Listening

  • Recognise familiar words about myself and my family when spoken slowly.
  • Understand numbers, prices and times said clearly.
02

Reading

  • Understand single words and very short, simple signs.
  • Read a name, a date and a price on a form or label.
03

Speaking

  • Introduce myself and use basic greetings and farewells.
  • Ask and answer simple questions about personal details.
04

Writing

  • Write my name, nationality and address on a form.
  • Write simple isolated words and very short phrases.
A1Breakthrough

A1 · Beginner

Learners can handle the basics of daily life. They talk about routines, possessions and immediate needs using simple present-tense structures, if the other person speaks slowly and clearly.

Guided study60–100 hrsGSE range22–29
After completing the level

A1 End-of-Level Diagnostic

The complete scored diagnostic and production rubric are still in preparation.

Evidence of progress

The learner notices, chooses, builds, understands, and produces language across grammar, vocabulary, receptive skills, and real communication.

By the end of A1, a learner can…

  • Understand and use familiar everyday expressions and basic phrases.
  • Introduce myself and others and ask about personal details.
  • Interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly.
  • Describe my home, routine and possessions in simple terms.
Aa

Grammar

Present simple (all forms, do / does)→Present continuous→there is / there are→have got→can for ability and permission→Adverbs of frequency→Prepositions of time and place→some / any with countable & uncountable nouns→Object pronouns→Imperatives→was / were (past of to be)→
¶

Vocabulary & Topics

Daily routines & telling the time→Jobs & workplaces→Food & drink→Rooms & furniture→Hobbies & free time→Clothes & shopping→Weather & seasons→Common verbs & adjectives→
01

Listening

  • Follow speech that is very slow and carefully articulated.
  • Understand simple directions and instructions.
02

Reading

  • Understand short, simple texts a single phrase at a time.
  • Get the gist of simple notices, menus and timetables.
03

Speaking

  • Ask and answer questions about everyday routines.
  • Make simple transactions in shops, cafés and stations.
04

Writing

  • Write short, simple notes and messages.
  • Write a simple postcard or fill in a detailed form.
A2Waystage

A2 · Elementary

Learners cope with routine tasks and exchanges. They can talk about the past and the future, compare things, and describe their background and immediate environment in short connected sentences.

Guided study100–200 hrsGSE range30–42
After completing the level

A2 End-of-Level Diagnostic

The complete scored diagnostic and production rubric are still in preparation.

Evidence of progress

The learner notices, chooses, builds, understands, and produces language across grammar, vocabulary, receptive skills, and real communication.

By the end of A2, a learner can…

  • Understand sentences and frequent expressions of immediate relevance.
  • Communicate in simple, routine tasks needing direct exchange of information.
  • Describe my background, environment and immediate needs.
  • Tell a simple story about past events and experiences.
Aa

Grammar

Past simple (regular & irregular verbs)→Past continuous→be going to for plans→will for predictions & offers→Comparatives & superlatives→Present perfect (ever / never, just / already / yet)→Modals: should, must, have to→Quantifiers: much / many / a lot of→First conditional→Adverbs of manner→Verb + infinitive / -ing→
¶

Vocabulary & Topics

Travel & transport→Health & the body→Town & directions→Past-time expressions→Feelings & personality→Technology & devices→Education & study→Phrasal verbs (common)→
01

Listening

  • Understand phrases about areas of immediate personal relevance.
  • Catch the main point in short, clear messages and announcements.
02

Reading

  • Read short, simple texts and find specific information.
  • Understand everyday signs, ads and short personal letters.
03

Speaking

  • Handle short social exchanges without sustaining the conversation myself.
  • Describe my family, living conditions and educational background.
04

Writing

  • Write short, simple notes and a basic personal letter.
  • Connect sentences with simple linkers like and, but and because.
B1Threshold

B1 · Intermediate

The independent-user threshold. Learners deal with most situations while travelling, produce connected text on familiar topics, and explain their opinions, plans and experiences.

Guided study200–350 hrsGSE range43–58
After completing the level

B1 End-of-Level Diagnostic

The complete scored diagnostic and production rubric are still in preparation.

Evidence of progress

The learner notices, chooses, builds, understands, and produces language across grammar, vocabulary, receptive skills, and real communication.

By the end of B1, a learner can…

  • Understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters.
  • Deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling.
  • Produce simple connected text on topics of personal interest.
  • Describe experiences, events, dreams, hopes and ambitions.
Aa

Grammar

Present perfect continuousSoonPast perfectSoonSecond conditionalSoonused to / would for past habitsSoonPassive voice (present & past simple)SoonReported speech (statements)SoonDefining relative clausesSoonModals of deduction: might, could, mustSoonQuestion tagsSoonGerunds vs infinitivesSoonFuture review: will / going to / present continuousSoon

Vocabulary & Topics

Work & careersSoonEnvironment & natureSoonMedia & newsSoonRelationshipsSoonMoney & spendingSoonCrime & societySoonCollocations & word familiesSoonDiscourse linkersSoon
01

Listening

  • Follow the main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters.
  • Understand the information in many radio or TV programmes.
02

Reading

  • Understand texts with everyday or job-related language.
  • Grasp the description of events, feelings and wishes in letters.
03

Speaking

  • Enter unprepared into conversation on familiar topics.
  • Narrate a story and describe reactions, hopes and ambitions.
04

Writing

  • Write straightforward connected text on familiar subjects.
  • Write personal letters describing experiences and impressions.
B2Vantage

B2 · Upper-Intermediate

Learners interact with fluency and spontaneity. They understand complex and abstract texts, argue a point of view, and write clear, detailed prose across a wide range of subjects.

Guided study350–600 hrsGSE range59–75
After completing the level

B2 End-of-Level Diagnostic

The complete scored diagnostic and production rubric are still in preparation.

Evidence of progress

The learner notices, chooses, builds, understands, and produces language across grammar, vocabulary, receptive skills, and real communication.

By the end of B2, a learner can…

  • Understand the main ideas of complex text on concrete and abstract topics.
  • Interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity with native speakers.
  • Produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects.
  • Explain a viewpoint, giving the advantages and disadvantages.
Aa

Grammar

Third & mixed conditionalsSoonPast perfect continuousSoonFull passive (all tenses, passive reporting)SoonReported speech (questions, commands, reporting verbs)SoonNon-defining relative clausesSoonModals of past speculation (must have, can't have)Soonwish / if onlySoonCausative have / get something doneSoonFuture perfect & future continuousSoonCleft sentences for emphasisSoonAdvanced discourse markersSoon
¶

Vocabulary & Topics

Abstract & academic topicsSoonPolitics & global issuesSoonScience & innovationSoonIdioms & fixed expressionsSoonRegister & formalitySoonNuanced adjectives & intensifiersSoonPhrasal verbs (advanced)SoonConnotation & shades of meaningSoon
01

Listening

  • Understand extended speech and follow complex lines of argument.
  • Understand most TV news, documentaries and films in standard speech.
02

Reading

  • Read articles and reports on contemporary problems and viewpoints.
  • Understand contemporary literary prose at a comfortable pace.
03

Speaking

  • Interact fluently enough to make regular conversation feel effortless.
  • Present clear, detailed arguments and develop a point of view.
04

Writing

  • Write clear, detailed text on a range of subjects in my field.
  • Write essays or reports, evaluating ideas and weighing evidence.
